text.p: Unemployment in Colombia's seven largest cities stood at 11.5 percent in December, the National Statistics Department said Monday.
The figure, issued quarterly, is down from 11.9 percent in September but up from 9.5 percent in December 1995.

A spokesman for the National Statistics Department blamed the year-on-year rise on recession in the labor-intensive construction industry and on the overall economic slump in 1996, when gross domestic product grew just 3.0 percent compared to 5.28 percent in 1995.
"The construction industry has been particularly hard hit, although the financial sector has expanded slightly. Public sector employment has remained about the same," the spokesman said.
The overall number of unemployed people in the country's seven largest cities is just over 700,000, according to National Statistics Department figures.
